name: ExecuTorch
notable_features: ExecuTorch is PyTorch's official on-device inference engine, announced 2024
Uses .pt2 export format via torch.export - models are exported from PyTorch, not converted from other formats
Supports Android (NNAPI, QNN), iOS (CoreML), and Linux embedded targets
Quantization: supports int8, int4, and uint8 quantization via PyTorch quantization tools
Delegation to hardware backends: CoreML (Apple Neural Engine), NNAPI (Android), QNN (Qualcomm), Vulkan (GPU)
Part of the PyTorch ecosystem - seamless transition from training to on-device deployment
hardware_caveats: .pt2 format is PyTorch-specific - no GGUF, ONNX, or safetensors support without conversion
LLM support is early - fewer optimized kernels than llama.cpp for transformer architectures
No continuous batching or paged KV cache - single-stream inference only
Delegation coverage varies by platform - not all ops are delegated to hardware backends
Smaller community and ecosystem than llama.cpp for local LLM inference
best_for: PyTorch users who want to deploy models on-device without leaving the PyTorch ecosystem
Android apps using NNAPI or QNN for hardware acceleration
iOS apps using CoreML for Neural Engine acceleration
Models already in PyTorch format that need mobile deployment
avoid_for: Non-PyTorch models - conversion to PyTorch is required
Maximum performance on Apple Silicon - MLX is faster on Metal
High-concurrency serving - no batching or scheduling support
Models only available in GGUF format
notes: ExecuTorch is the newest entry in the on-device inference space, backed by PyTorch/Meta. Its main advantage is seamless PyTorch integration - models can be exported and deployed without format conversion. However, the LLM ecosystem is less mature than llama.cpp, and the .pt2 format is PyTorch-specific. For local LLM inference, MLX (Apple) or llama.cpp (cross-platform) are currently better choices, but ExecuTorch is the right choice for PyTorch-centric workflows. ||| MAINTENANCE (dated fact, GitHub API, 2026-10-04): last commit 2026-10-04 (0.0 months before this record), latest release v1.5.1 published 2026-09-23, 626 contributors (distinct committers including anonymous), open_issues_count 1309 (issues PLUS pull requests - see [[ev-github-open-issues-count-includes-pull-requests]]), not archived, 5078 stars.
